expectations.text: The reply says plainly that little research or few sources that meet the bar exist on this exact question (or on parts of it).
expectations.evidence: "Very thin: I found no study of four-day weeks and marching bands. On band numbers, your second sub-question, I found nothing at all."

expectations.text: The reply suggests at least one specific place or person to look further, such as a library database, a librarian, music education organizations, or band directors.
expectations.evidence: "ERIC and RILM (a music literature database) are worth searching. A librarian can also get you sources 2–4 in full." and "Band directors in four-day districts"

expectations.text: Every source the reply presents is a peer-reviewed article, a scholarly book, a report or data from a government or international agency, a report from an established research organization, a preprint labeled as not yet peer reviewed, a doctoral dissertation (not a master's thesis) labeled as not peer reviewed, or a reputable news outlet (or a primary source labeled as one). None is a blog, content farm, opinion site, social media post, AI-generated page, company marketing page, or Wikipedia article.
expectations.evidence: Every source is in an allowed category: the peer-reviewed articles, the RAND/HEDCO/NCSL reports, "Dissertation, not peer reviewed", "Primary source (state rules body)" and an Iowa Public Radio news article. None is a blog or similar.

expectations.text: Every link in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session. Every DOI (as a doi.org link or as text) either was opened itself or appears exactly in the list of DOIs found on pages Claude opened (shown under FILES or DOIS ON OPENED PAGES). A DOI seen only in search results doesn't count.
expectations.evidence: Every link was fetched: doi.org/10.7249/rr-a373-1, doi.org/10.1162/edfp_a_00316, doi.org/10.1080/09645292.2021.2006610, doi.org/10.1111/josh.12941, the HEDCO report page, digitalcommons.liberty.edu/doctoral/6700, the uiltexas page, the ncsl page and the iowapublicradio page.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: Only one question mark is directed at the user: "Which ones surprised you most?" The other prompts are instructions.
